I need to make a decision for the current Monopoly turn.

I have $444 cash and am on Indiana Avenue after paying $90 rent. I own a light blue monopoly with zero houses.

I need nine houses on the light blue set to maximize rent. That costs $450, but I only have $444. I will mortgage dead assets like Water Works and Mediterranean Avenue to raise the funds.

Mortgaging Water Works for $75 gives $519 cash. Nine houses cost $450, leaving $69. Mortgaging Mediterranean for $30 leaves only $24 after building. Water Works is the better choice for liquidity.

The rent jump from two to three houses on light blue is massive. Two houses yield $90/$90/$100, but three houses yield $270/$270/$300. I must reach three houses on every property in the set. I am also checking p3's dark blue holdings for comparison.

p3 has two houses on Park Place and three on Boardwalk. p1's red set shows Kentucky with two houses, Indiana with one, and Illinois with two. The $90 rent paid to p1 matches Indiana's single-house rate.

p2 owns the orange set with two houses on St. James and Tennessee, and three on New York. That three-house rent is $600, which is dangerous.

The current player order is p1 on B.O. Railroad, p2 on Virginia Avenue, p3 on Chance, and me on Indiana Avenue. I am about to end my turn.

The turn sequence is unclear. Turn 67 had p2 ending after a trade, then p3 collected GO and built. Turn 68 was p3's turn. Turn 69 is p4's turn. The exact player order is uncertain.

The standard turn order is p1, p2, p3, p4. After I end my turn, p1 will play next. p1 is on B&O Railroad, which sits behind the light blue properties, so they would need to travel almost the full board to reach them. I am also trying to identify which Chance space p3 occupies.

I am mapping the exact board positions to identify which Chance space p3 occupies. The first Chance sits after the Baltic and Income Tax area, while the Short Line and Park Place Chance is later in the sequence.

The Chance space sits between Oriental and Vermont. p3 is likely on that middle Chance, which would let them land on either light blue property on the very next roll.

The middle Chance between Oriental and Vermont is the most likely space. p3 already completed their turn, so they cannot land on my light blues this round.

I will mortgage Water Works for $75 to raise cash. I cannot build houses until after p1 and p2 move, so I must act now. Unmortgaging costs 10% interest on the mortgage value.

Unmortgaging Water Works costs $83, while Mediterranean costs $33. The larger cash buffer after building is worth the extra interest. Selling nine houses would return only $225, which is too little to cover New York's $600 rent or Park Place's $500. I will mortgage Water Works now and can unmortgage it later if needed.

I will not mortgage the light blue properties I am about to build on. I also will not mortgage States, Ventnor, Pacific, or North Carolina. These are partial monopolies or blockers that would lose their strategic value if mortgaged.

I will mortgage Water Works. I rejected building only eight houses now because the two-house property would still charge $90 or $100 instead of the full $270 or $300.

p1 cannot build more red houses. Indiana needs $150 and p1 only has $138.

p2 cannot build more orange houses either. St. James and Tennessee each need $100 for a third house, but p2 has only $134 and everything is mortgaged.

p3 also cannot build more dark blue houses. Park Place needs $200 and p3 has no cash.

Boardwalk at three houses costs $1400. That is lethal to every opponent.
